criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test binary`: a_nested_run_works_in_a_scratch_copy_with_fake_agents passes, and a companion test simulates low free space (below 10 GB) in the nested run's environment and still passes because the test config sets min_free_gb to 0.
criteria.evidence: All 15 tests passed. These include a_nested_run_works_in_a_scratch_copy_with_fake_agents, the companion a_nested_run_ignores_low_free_space_because_the_test_config_has_no_minimum (ATHENA_FREE_BYTES=9000000000, asserts exit 0 and the landing), and the control the_simulated_free_space_reaches_the_nested_run_when_a_minimum_is_set (min 10, asserts a non-zero exit and the 'environment: low disk: 9.0 GB free, 10.0 GB required' text).

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core disk`: the disk guard's tests still show a hold (job stays queued, 'environment: low disk') and a fail-fast with simulated low free space.
criteria.evidence: All 5 core disk unit tests passed, including the new a_simulated_reading_is_used_only_when_it_is_a_whole_number. The hold and fail-fast tests live in the athena-cli drain tests: low_disk_at_dispatch_that_cleanup_does_not_cure_holds_the_job_queued_and_not_rejected, low_disk_before_the_checks_fails_the_job_retryably_and_a_retry_with_space_runs_the_checks, and the_real_steps_hold_... . All of them passed, now using disk_fixture (minimum 10) with simulated_free/set_free readings.

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs test_config sets [disk] min_free_gb = 0 with a comment explaining why, and the production default (10 GB in athena-data config) is unchanged.
criteria.evidence:
Read in the diff: test_config appends "
[disk]
min_free_gb = 0
" with a comment saying tests must not depend on real free space and that the guard's own tests set a minimum with with_min_free_gb. The diff does not touch athena-data; config.rs still has DEFAULT_MIN_FREE_GB, and its tests assert min_free_gb() == 10.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: all pass, and no test in the suite reads the machine's real free disk to decide its result.
criteria.evidence: Athena's records: fmt passed, clippy passed, and cargo test passed (1282 tests). Code reading: in-process fixtures install plenty_of_space (common/mod.rs:169, test_support, run_pin_tests, scope_guard). Spawned binaries use configs derived from test_config, which sets min 0. The only real df read is the_real_reader_reports_some_space_..., which asserts only > 0.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry stating that tests no longer depend on real free disk space and how the minimum or free-space reading is set in tests.
criteria.evidence: A new bullet under Unreleased/Changed says that tests no longer depend on the machine's real free disk space, that test_config sets `[disk] min_free_gb = 0`, that guard tests use with_min_free_gb and simulated values, that ATHENA_FREE_BYTES replaces the reading in a spawned binary, and that the production default of 10 GB is unchanged.

findings.summary: The production binary honors a test-only environment override of the free-space reading.
findings.evidence: df_free_bytes returns ATHENA_FREE_BYTES whenever it parses as a number, in any build. If this variable is left set in an operator's environment, the real disk guard is silently bypassed. The accepted reading allowed this approach, but a cfg or a log line when it is used would make it safer.

findings.summary: The with_min_free_gb doc comment says it sets the minimum "whatever it was", but the function asserts the config contains `min_free_gb = 0`.

summary: The change does what was asked. The shared test config (test_config) now sets `[disk] min_free_gb = 0`, so CLI tests, including nested runs, no longer depend on the machine's real free disk space. disk.rs gains an `ATHENA_FREE_BYTES` override, which takes effect only when it holds a whole number, so a spawned binary can be shown a simulated free-space reading. A new companion test gives the nested ask/go 9 GB free and the run still lands. A control test sets a 10 GB minimum and fails with 'environment: low disk: 9.0 GB free, 10.0 GB required', which proves the simulated reading takes effect. The drain tests now set the 10 GB minimum explicitly through disk_fixture, and they still show the hold and the fail-fast under simulated values. The production default of 10 GB is unchanged. I ran the binary, core disk and drain low-disk tests myself, and all passed. The fmt, clippy and full test results come from Athena's records for this tree. Two small notes: the production binary now accepts a test-only environment variable that can override the guard, and one doc comment is inaccurate.
